newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Supply of funds runs high on Bulgaria depo market.
newsitem.headline: Supply of funds runs high on Bulgaria depo market.

text.p: Lev liquidity was high on Bulgaria's interbank deposit market on Friday due to mark sales and demand for funds was very low, dealers said.
"There is almost no demand on the interbank market. Demand for funds comes mainly from final customers who need levs to cover pending payments," a bank dealer said.
Traders said that banks which have bought marks at lower levels in the past several weeks are now selling them to the central bank to profit from forex transaction costs.
The central bank was buying marks at 995 levs and selling at 1,000 levs under a fixed exchange rate regime launched on Tuesday.
Overnight interbank depo rates stood at 9-10 percent annually, flat from Thursday, while deposits for up to seven days were borrowed at a simple annual interest of 7-8 ercent, also unchanged.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 9.50 percent on Thursday from 9.00 percent on Wednesday, a central bank official said.

The simple annual main interest rate is now set at 10.12 percent by the central bank. The central bank said it will cut its main rate to 9.76 percent annual from July 7. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
